title: The approval item and its two records: the raise operation, the action and answer shapes, the routing and final-call value sets, the message texts and the login name have no source
source: FSD P7 Decision center and log v3 A2.15 Route a recommendation to the approver by limit, A2.16 Approve inside the limit, A2.18 Reject a recommendation with a reason, A2.23 Show the approval queue and A2.24 Apply the delegation of authority limits against TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 T3.1 approval and decision_log_entry, T3.2 LOV-APPROVAL-STATUS, T-A.1 API-P7-002 to API-P7-008 and T-A.2; legacy RWB-E6-028 metadata table, Endpoints, Screen and states and Validation and messages; Architecture v5 slides 14, 20, 28 and 41
description: Seven values of this story are fixed by no source. (1) The raise of an approval has no path and no method: TSD P7 v2 T-A.1 publishes only the reads API-P7-002 and API-P7-008, the three decisions API-P7-003 to API-P7-005, the two ledger reads API-P7-006 and API-P7-007, and the Ownership Map publishes GET /approvals only, so the operation the write-off story calls to hand the item over is not published anywhere. (2) The T-A.2 answers name ApprovalPage, ApprovalDetail, ApprovalAction, DecisionLogPage and DecisionLogEntry without a field set, so neither the request nor the answer of any of the eight operations is written out. (3) The value sets are partly open: the content of LOV-DECISION is not enumerated in any source this story may read, so the decision code of the escalation and of the sale selection is not fixed; final_call is a varchar(40) with no list, so the call of a routing record and the calls APPROVED, RETURNED and REFUSED are not fixed; the value set of approval.source_type is not given; and the base value of approval.escalation_level is not given. (4) The states beyond LOV-APPROVAL-STATUS: the list gives WAITING, HELD_NO_LIMIT, APPROVED, REFUSED and RETURNED and nothing for an escalated, withdrawn or re-opened item, while FSD P7 v3 A2.19 and A2.20 move an item to a higher role and raise escalation_level inside WAITING; the legacy screen states scan, proposed, in committee and approved are SCR-27's and not the item's. (5) The texts: MSG-P7-009, MSG-P7-010 and MSG-P7-011 are named by FSD P7 v3 A2.15, A2.16 and A2.20 and written out nowhere, and no message id exists for a raise refused for a missing source item or for an item that is no longer WAITING, so the story reuses MSG-GEN-001 and MSG-GEN-004. (6) The parameter and message identifiers beyond MSG-P7-003 and MSG-S7-001: the due time of an item, the escalation window and the page size of the two reads are named as values by FSD P7 v3 A2.15 and A2.20 and as parameter rows by no source. (7) The name of the per-service database login of DP-02.
evidence: TSD P7 v2 T-A.1 lists API-P7-002 GET /approvals, API-P7-003 POST /approvals/{approvalId}/approve, API-P7-004 POST /approvals/{approvalId}/return, API-P7-005 POST /approvals/{approvalId}/refuse, API-P7-006 GET /decision-log, API-P7-007 GET /decision-log/{entryId} and API-P7-008 GET /approvals/{approvalId}, and no operation that creates an approval; T-A.2 gives a Purpose, a Request keyword, a Response name and an error list per operation and no field set; TSD P7 v2 T3.1 types decision_code varchar(8) against LOV-DECISION and final_call varchar(40) with no list and gives escalation_level integer with no base value; TSD P7 v2 T3.2 enumerates LOV-APPROVAL-STATUS as WAITING, HELD_NO_LIMIT, APPROVED, REFUSED and RETURNED only; FSD P7 v3 A2.15 AC-EXC-P7-015-06 and A2.24 AC-EXC-P7-024-11 name MSG-P7-010 and A2.20 names MSG-P7-011 without their texts; legacy RWB-E6-028 lists MSG-S7-001, MSG-GEN-001, MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P7-003 and no other identifier; Architecture v5 slide 41 gives every service its own login and no login name
area: Approval contract, approval value sets, message standard and P7 rwb-decision configuration
owner_role: Business analyst, P7 rwb-decision, with the P4 rwb-access business analyst and the S7 rwb-writeoff analyst
proposed: Agree the raise as POST /approvals on the decision base with a body carrying caseId, decisionCode, regulationItem, capabilityArea, productGroup, amount, sourceType, sourceRef, ruleId, ruleVersion and an Idempotency-Key; agree ApprovalAction as a reason-bearing body and ApprovalPage and DecisionLogPage as items, page, size and total; read the decision code and the final calls as reference data of LOV-DECISION and of the final-call list with the version in force; keep the five LOV-APPROVAL-STATUS values and carry the escalation inside WAITING through escalation_level; write the texts of MSG-P7-009, MSG-P7-010 and MSG-P7-011 in the message standard; and name the login in the ACE DB allocation of wave 1.

title: The DP table adds two platform contracts and the story consumes three operations that its metadata rows do not carry
source: Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP table rows DP-03, DP-13 and DP-19; section R5.4 dependency classes; the metadata rows Depends on (build) = None, Contract dependencies = RWB-S7-E6028-CON, Integration dependencies = None, External dependencies = None; the Ownership Map api rows GET /approvals, GET /approvals/{approvalId}, POST /approvals/{approvalId}/approve, .../return, .../refuse, GET /decision-log and GET /decision-log/{entryId} to P7 and GET /me/session to P4; Architecture v5 slide 14 (rwb-access IN: POST /authorise, GET /doa-limits; P7 OUT: REST Access: DoA limits) and slide 41
section: Sections 3, 12.2, 12.8 and 13 of the story, Pattern application; the metadata table and the fragment
description: The patterns of this key add two contracts that are absent from the metadata rows: H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON from DP-03 (the local decision-record library and rwb.decision-record.v1) and H RWB-PLT-N001-CON from DP-19 (the gateway-bff composite route). Four consumed dependencies are named by no pattern and by no metadata row: the P4 delegation-limit answer the routing level is read from, the P4 authorise call the reads and the three decisions are guarded by, the P3 case read the scope filter is applied to, and the reference-data list values of LOV-DECISION, LOV-CAPABILITY, LOV-APPROVAL-LEVEL, LOV-APPROVAL-STATUS and LOV-PRODUCT, because DP-07 is not among the patterns of this key and the Ownership Map publishes no row for the authorise or the delegation path. None of the six blocks the build beyond Day 1 — the two platform contracts are platform CON stories of wave 0 and the others are published contracts of P3 and P4 or their fakes — but a reader of the metadata alone would conclude the story needs nothing, and the Dependency Map and the Day-1 allocation cannot see them.
evidence: Template and Rules v1 R5.5: DP-03 adds H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and DP-19 adds H RWB-PLT-N001-CON; R5.7 rule 2 makes a C dependency non-blocking and rule 3 keeps an H to the same service or a platform CON story; the metadata rows of this story name None and RWB-S7-E6028-CON; the fragment H is empty and C holds RWB-S7-E6028-CON only; the Ownership Map publishes GET /approvals, GET /approvals/{approvalId}, the three decisions, GET /decision-log and GET /decision-log/{entryId} with owner P7 and publishes GET /me/session with owner P4 and no row for the authorise or the delegation path; Architecture v5 slide 14 gives P4 IN POST /authorise and GET /doa-limits and gives P7 OUT REST Access: DoA limits; TSD P7 v2 T3.2 carries the five lists
area: Dependency map and build sequencing, P7 rwb-decision
owner_role: Solution architect, P7 rwb-decision, with the platform team and the rwb-access team
proposed: Carry the two platform H dependencies and the four consumed contracts in the Dependency Map as non-blocking platform contracts of wave 0 and published contracts of P3 and P4, built against their fakes; leave the metadata rows as the plan gives them and cite this row in section 13 of the story.

title: One escalation leaves two decision entries, the routing record of rwb-decision and the write-off record of rwb-writeoff, and no source says so plainly
source: Architecture v5 slide 20 (every service writes its own decision_record and publishes DecisionRecorded on rwb.decision-record.v1) and slide 28 (recorded locally at once, then sealed centrally within 5 minutes, strict mode only at the four points of no return); FSD P7 Decision center and log v3 A2.15 AC-P7-015-01 (a routing entry records the rule, the version and the route parameter) and A2.2 Write a decision log entry for every decision; legacy RWB-E6-028 AC2 and its Data table on decision_log_entry and rule_row; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-WO-12 and R-WO-13; RWB-ITG-E6028-ITG section 4 step 11 and section 8 BR8
section: Sections 1, 4, 7 (AC1, AC8), 8 (BR4, BR10), 9 and 11 of the story
description: Rule R-WO-12 is one step of one case: the pack goes to the credit approval committee and the case moves to ESCALATED_TO_CREDIT_COMMITTEE. Two records can be written for it and no source settles the count. On the reading of Architecture v5 slides 20 and 28 the state change is S7's, so rwb-writeoff writes the local record of R-WO-12 and publishes it on rwb.decision-record.v1, and rwb-decision collects it into the central ledger; on the reading of FSD P7 v3 A2.15 the routing of the item writes a routing entry of its own in rwb-decision with the rule, the version and the route parameter. Both readings are consistent with the sources, so one escalation may leave one entry or two, and a reader of the ledger cannot tell a duplicate from a pair without a rule. The same question applies to R-WO-32 on the sale selection, where the record is S7's and the approval item it follows is P7's.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 20 'DB Own schema: business tables + outbox + inbox + decision_record' and 'EVT DecisionRecorded to rwb.decision-record.v1 (ledger in rwb-decision)'; Architecture v5 slide 28 'Saved with the change; Collected centrally'; FSD P7 v3 A2.15 AC-P7-015-01 'the routing entry records rule R-LIT-03, version LIT-2026.12 and route parameter rwb.approval.route.D7.1.role'; FSD P7 v3 A2.2 'Write a decision log entry for every decision'; legacy RWB-E6-028 AC2 'route the pack to the credit approval committee ... the case moves to ESCALATED_TO_CREDIT_COMMITTEE' with no count of entries; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-WO-12 and R-WO-13
area: Decision record scope and ledger content, P7 rwb-decision with S7 rwb-writeoff
owner_role: Solution architect, P7 rwb-decision, with the S7 rwb-writeoff solution architect and the internal audit lead
proposed: Keep both records and make the pair explicit: the write-off record names the state change and the rule that fired, the routing record names the level, the delegation row and the limit version the pack was routed at, neither repeats the other's facts, and the ledger read returns them in chain order so an auditor sees the pair as one step. State the reading in the ledger documentation of the service before the wave entry check.

title: The right and the role that may approve an escalated write-off pack are read two ways
source: TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 T-A.1 (API-P7-002 to API-P7-005 and API-P7-008 declare access Decision log, right A) against T6.1 RBAC matrix (every role listed with R on the Decision log column and no A); legacy RWB-E6-028 Permission checks (Write-off and posting right A held by RW-CREDITAD, RW-PRODHEAD, RW-WOCOMM and RW-FINANCE); FSD P7 Decision center and log v3 A2.16.3.3 and A2.19.3.3 (the credit approval committee member as an also-user of approve and of escalate); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-WO-12 (the credit approval committee chaired by the product head with Risk); TSD P7 v2 T3.2 LOV-CAPABILITY (WRITE_OFF_AND_POSTING)
section: Sections 1, 3, 5 (X7), 7 (AC2, AC4), 8 (BR5, BR12), 10 and 14 of the story
description: Two questions about authority have two answers each. First, the right: TSD P7 v2 T-A.1 declares the Decision log right A on the approval read and on the three decisions, while the RBAC matrix of the same document lists every role with R on the Decision log column and no role with A, and the legacy story guards the same actions with the Write-off and posting capability area at right A. Second, the role: rule R-WO-12 routes the pack to the credit approval committee chaired by the product head with Risk, FSD P7 v3 A2.16 and A2.19 name the credit approval committee member as a user of approve and escalate, and the legacy permission table of RWB-E6-028 gives Write-off and posting A to RW-CREDITAD, RW-PRODHEAD, RW-WOCOMM and RW-FINANCE and does not list RW-CREDCOMM, the credit approval committee member. A story that follows one source alone will either let the committee member the rule routes to past the guard, or let a role the legacy table excludes decide the pack.
evidence: TSD P7 v2 T-A.1 rows API-P7-002, API-P7-003, API-P7-004, API-P7-005 and API-P7-008 'Decision log A'; TSD P7 v2 T6.1 columns Role and Decision log, every row R, no A; legacy RWB-E6-028 Permission checks 'Write-off and posting | A | RW-CREDITAD, RW-PRODHEAD, RW-WOCOMM, RW-FINANCE'; FSD P7 v3 A2.16.3.3 and A2.19.3.3 'Credit approval committee member | Also uses'; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-WO-12 action 'Route the pack to the credit approval committee chaired by the product head with Risk'; TSD P7 v2 T3.2 LOV-CAPABILITY 'WRITE_OFF_AND_POSTING'
area: Authority, rights and role model, P7 rwb-decision with P4 rwb-access and S7 rwb-writeoff
owner_role: P4 rwb-access business analyst and the security administrator, with the P7 rwb-decision business analyst
proposed: Read the Decision log right A of T-A.1 as the right on the approval operations and the FSD P7 v3 T6.1 column as the read right only; carry the capability area WRITE_OFF_AND_POSTING on the approval row and require both in the authorise answer; and add RW-CREDCOMM to the holders of the capability right in the P4 role model, or record why the rule routes to a role that cannot decide, before the wave entry check.
